This Fifth Wheel Prototype Does Everything Differently, Stays on Budget
25 photos
Photo: YouTube/All About RVs
Fall 2026 is really starting to feel like a turning point for the 2027 RV-ing season, what with the surprises in store from established manufacturers and new companies, new models, new construction methods, and new design ideas. This brand new fifth wheel RV would fall in that last category.
This is the 2027 Salem Hemisphere 383WDRK, which will also be sold under the Wildwood Heritage Glen 383WDRK name with differences only in terms of exterior and interior badging. It's a brand new floorplan in the Salem Hemisphere/Heritage Glen series, with a layout that's not necessarily new but it's interpreted in a way that you won't find anywhere else.
Both the Salem and the Wildwood brands operate under the Forest River umbrella, so this new floorplan was on display at the recent Dealer Expo, as a prototype. Content creator Ray from All About RVs says that he was personally involved in its development and that some things are bound to change inside before it goes into production, which is standard fare in the industry.
His video tour offers a much better appreciation of what makes this unit different from all the rest , better than the one posted by Forest River Direct, which you will also find at the bottom of the page.
Photo: Forest River The 383WDRK is a four-slide fifth wheel with a washer-dryer and a rear kitchen layout. Ray says that it's actually based on a popular but more expensive model from a different company, and that this is Forest River's more budget-friendly interpretation of it. That said, don't take budget-friendly to mean cheap or compromising: this RV is as nice as they get, with high quality finishes and a lot of focus on comfort and style.
As the headline says, the 383WDRK does everything differently, from the way it uses slide-outs to expand the available footprint to how it tries to think outside the box in the design of RV staples like a freestanding dinette or a half-bath. The result is a fifth wheel that oozes style and a surprising amount of functionality.
Coming in at 43 feet 9 inches (13.3 meters) of total length, the 383WDRK rides on a tandem axle and, as already noted, has four slide-outs in total, all of them flush within the floor and offered with marine-type woven carpeting. Not much is known about construction , except from what Ray says about the sidewalls being aluminum studded, foam block insulated, and with a layer of fiberglass painted in two tones of gray on the outside.
Photo: Forest River Direct You can see that the underbelly is fully enclosed and presumably heated, and all holding tanks have 12V heating pads on them. That means that this is a four-season RV, so it's perfect for extended vacations or even full-time living.
At the first look, the layout is typical for a fifth wheel: a front bedroom with a ensuite bathroom and a walk-in wardrobe in that front cap, and a rear kitchen that spills into the mid living room. The execution, though, is different from everything else.
For instance, the cooking block in the kitchen is in a smaller slide-out, so that it's recessed from the actual kitchen space, which feels larger because of this. The super-slide on the campsite side holds a massive dual-door stainless steel fridge with freezer, a pantry with sensor lights and plenty of space, and a dedicated coffee station. Nearby is a legless dining table mounted on the wall horizontally, so you can choose which view you want to look out on: the TV in the living room or the view out on the campsite.
Photo: Forest River Direct The living room is shown in the prototype with a loveseat/pull-out sofa in another small slide and a pair of theater seats with recliner function, right in front of the entertainment wall with the TV and the fireplace. This won't be the final design, though, because the theater seats are too bulky and take up too much space when the slides are closed, so the whole arrangement will probably be replaced by an L-shaped sectional sofa.
In front of the entrance is the "WD" part in the 838WDRK name, the washer-dryer laundry station. It's located in a half bath that's surprisingly elegant and spacious, with a round stainless steel sink and open storage, a porcelain toilet, and a stacked washer and dryer under more cabinets. This isn't a full-on laundry station, but it's the closest thing.
The main bedroom is on the upper deck, with a king bed with a large storage compartment underneath, a dresser with an integrated vanity table that all women will simply love , and prep for a second TV. From here, you move into the ensuite bathroom – a generously sized space with dual vanities, solid surface counters, an oversize mirror, a porcelain toilet, a linen closet, and a large one-piece fiberglass shower with glass doors and a skylight.
Photo: Forest River Direct The full wardrobe is at the very front, and again, it's bound to be a ladies' favorite. Featuring a wraparound hanging rod, another dresser with drawers, a bench, and deep cubbies for shoe storage, it's a walk-in space where fashion will feel right at home. Sorry not sorry.
Storage outside includes a front compartment for the batteries and the spare wheel, a cavernous pass-through with several points of access, and a nice storage solution for fishing rods.
Standard features will include an 18,000-BTU Furrion Chill Cube AC in the living room, a ducted 15,000-BTU one in the bedroom, an on-demand water heater, a furnace, GE residential appliances, and two power awnings with LED lights. Also standard is 6-point electric auto-leveling, a 200W solar panel on the roof, full-length barreled ceilings, and square windows with built-in shades and thermafoil reflective backing.
Photo: Forest River Direct Most specs are still listed as TBD ("to be determined") as of this writing, but dry weight will be at around 14,300 lbs (6.486 kg). Retail price is almost $125,000, with Ray mentioning a minimum advertised pricing of $77,499.
Forest River and the entire team are still taking feedback on this floorplan, so there's no word yet on when it might arrive at dealerships.
